subject.title: fix(codex): cap managed app-server trace logs

question: Should managed Codex trace retention be owned by an OpenClaw enabled-by-default file cap with three environment controls, or by upgrading and relying on Codex's native row-retention policy?
rationale: Both approaches can bound storage, but they establish different long-term ownership, configuration, pruning, and upgrade contracts that cannot be selected safely from implementation correctness alone.

options.title: Prefer Native Codex Retention
options.body: Verify retention in the pinned or next managed Codex release and upgrade the pin if needed, avoiding a parallel OpenClaw file-rotation policy unless production measurements still show unbounded growth.

options.title: Accept OpenClaw Retention
options.body: Rebase the branch, confirm the 512 MiB and two-snapshot defaults, and add fresh-install and upgrade proof for the enabled-by-default storage behavior.

options.title: Pause Pending Upstream Release
options.body: Keep the incident open but pause or close this PR until a Codex release with the native retention implementation can be measured in an OpenClaw-managed home.

recommendation.title: Prefer Native Codex Retention
recommendation.body: Verify retention in the pinned or next managed Codex release and upgrade the pin if needed, avoiding a parallel OpenClaw file-rotation policy unless production measurements still show unbounded growth.

likelyOwner.reason: They performed the most direct review and implementation work on the retention ownership, active-home safety, and defaults in the available history.
